title: Water Quality Test Report
key_sentences: The sample complied with the drinking water standards for all the parameters tested, except for lead.
The lead concentration of 14 µg/L exceeds the prescribed limit of 10 µg/L.
This is most likely caused by lead pipework within the building rather than by the public supply.
We recommend the following actions while the source of the lead is investigated.
A repeat sample taken after flushing would show whether the lead comes from water standing in the pipes.
All samples were kept chilled and analysed within 24 hours of collection.

list_items.text: Run the kitchen tap for at least two minutes before drawing water for drinking or cooking, especially after the building has been unused overnight.
Use only the kitchen tap for drinking water until the pipework has been surveyed.
Ask a plumber to identify and replace any lead pipes or fittings between the stopcock and the kitchen.
Request a follow-up sample after any remedial work.
